Golomb rulers: LLM proposer versus classical search, at a matched budget of verifier calls

At a matched budget of verifier calls, does an LLM proposing Golomb rulers as data match the known optimal lengths (OEIS A003022) as often as a classical randomized search, on development orders n = 8-11 and sealed orders n = 12-13 — and is a match search or recall?

study: 24-golomb-llm-vs-search · metric: optima_matched (search), optima_matched (llm) · domain: combinatorial search (Golomb rulers) · 2026-11-03

1. The Question 2. The Method 3. The Data 4. The Journey 5. Findings 6. Coding Advice 7. Next Steps

What you will take away

  • At a matched number of verifier calls, the LLM arm matched the tabulated length on more development pairs than the classical search did (6 of 12 against 0 of 12), and on the sealed orders neither arm matched (0 of 6 each). The development contrast is a count difference on two orders, not an established rate (claims C2, C3).
  • The recall signature that was registered (a match already in the first proposal batch) was not seen: 1 of 12 pairs, with the other matches arriving after verifier feedback (claim C4). That refutes the registered rule; it does not exclude recall.
  • Every verdict is the verifier's number, not the searcher's, and every matched ruler re-attains a length that OEIS A003022 already lists. The study establishes nothing new about any Golomb ruler (claim C16).

The referee's verdict on this study covers the study record (findings.md, the lock, the predictions). It was given before any figure or tutorial existed, so it does not cover this page or its figures. The page reads its records from the lock and the state file (section 5 prints them) and has had its own mechanical checks, which are not a second referee.

The decision this study informs

Claims that a language model “found an optimal combinatorial object” are now common. A reader weighing one needs two things the headline rarely gives: who checked the object, and whether the model searched or remembered. This study builds the smallest honest test of both. The object is the Golomb ruler: integer marks on a ruler such that every pairwise distance occurs once. The shortest ruler for each is tabulated in OEIS A003022 and in public tables, so the answer key is printed in the textbook.

The question, as registered in study.yaml:

At a matched budget of verifier calls, does an LLM proposing Golomb rulers as data match the known tabulated lengths as often as a classical randomized search, on development orders 8–11 and sealed orders 12–13, and is a match search or recall?

The decision the answer feeds is practical: should a claimed LLM match on a combinatorial benchmark be read as search, as recall, or as neither until a control says otherwise?

The design in one picture

PieceWhat it is
InstanceOrders 8–11 (development, 12 pairs of order and trial) and orders 12–13 (sealed, 6 pairs), three trials per order. Each pair gets 2000 candidate evaluations.
Arm 1 — search trackRandomized construction plus simulated annealing, in search.py.
Arm 2 — llm trackThe dated snapshot qwen-flash-2025-07-28 proposes 10 rulers per request as JSON data, never code, for 200 requests, each told the verifier's verdicts on its previous batch.
JudgeOne declared verifier, verify.py, outside the mutable surface and hashed at the METHOD gate. It recomputes every count from the artifact with integer arithmetic.
Metricoptima_matched: the number of pairs whose best verified ruler has the tabulated length. An exact integer; resolution 1.
Registered rulesFive predictions (P1 to P5), each an arithmetic rule adjudicated by the notary, not by prose.

Both tracks are registered: every run is a pre-declared cell that is measured, not a climb with keeps and discards. That shapes section 4.

Intuition: an exam whose answer key is in the textbook

A student who writes the right answer in the first minute has shown you they read the book. A student who gets there after twenty crossed-out attempts may have worked it out, or half-remembered it and fixed the details. The grader is a stencil: it tells right from wrong without knowing how either student got there. Here the answer key is OEIS A003022 (ref:oeis_a003022), the stencil is verify.py, and the two students are an annealer and a language model.

The asymmetry that makes verifier-guided search work is that checking a ruler is cheap and finding a short one is not. Checking takes subtractions and a duplicate test. The tabulated lengths exist because other people ran exhaustive searches, one order at a time (ref:robinson1979, ref:robinson1983, ref:shearer1990). Any proposer may guess; one small checker, written once and never edited by the search, decides.

A pretrained model is not a blind proposer here, because the answers are public. An ML researcher knows this as test-set contamination. So the sharper question is not “does the LLM match more often?” but “when it matches, did it search or remember?” The instrument chosen for that is the timing of a match: a match in the very first batch, before any verifier feedback exists, is what recall predicts.

The load-bearing math

A candidate with and length is valid when all pairwise differences are distinct. This is the same as the Sidon condition (ref:wikipedia_sidon), by the rearrangement :

Everything is integer arithmetic, so the check is exact and has no tolerance to choose. With both ends fixed at and , a proposer aiming at length faces a set of candidates of size

and an unpruned certificate of the tabulated length would have to rule out every shorter ruler, of them by the hockey-stick identity. Real exhaustive searches prune hard, but the counts show why each order was its own result. A blind uniform draw at the tabulated length matches with chance ( is the number of tabulated rulers up to reflection), which falls to the order of by order 13 (method card table).

The study's metric is a match count decided by the verifier alone. With budget candidates per pair and the -th candidate an arm submits:

The verifier aborts a run if any verified ruler is shorter than (the table or the checker would be wrong), so means “equal to the tabulated length”, never “beat it”. For the figures, the gap of a pair is

and a match is a gap of exactly 0.

What is matched and what is not. The budget is matched in candidate evaluations, which are verifier calls. The annealer submits one candidate at a time and sees a verdict on each. The LLM submits 10 per request (200 requests) and sees one text block of 10 verdicts. Wall-clock, tokens, information per step and, above all, each proposer's prior are not matched. The unmatched prior is the confound the study exists to expose.

The recall signature

The registered signature is , the number of LLM pairs whose first proposal batch already holds a verified ruler of length . By the verifier's rules . The method card bounds the chance that a blind proposer hits in its first batch by with , tiny at every lane order, so a first-batch hit would be strong evidence of an informed proposer. It would still not separate retrieval of a table from any other structured prior.

The two arms

  • Classical search. Start from a random ruler with ends fixed and interior marks drawn at random, aim one length below the best valid ruler, and anneal the interior marks to remove repeated differences (ref:kirkpatrick1983 supplies the acceptance rule). A candidate is a mark list; every call to the private checker spends one evaluation.
  • LLM as proposer of data. In the style of ref:opro2024: the model returns a JSON list of 10 lists of integers, the checker's verdicts on that batch go into the next prompt, and nothing is ever repaired. A missing or unparseable entry still spends its evaluation, so malformed output is not free. The design deliberately differs from FunSearch and AlphaEvolve (ref:funsearch2024, ref:alphaevolve2025), which evolve programs, not objects.

When it pays, when it does not

A matched-budget design on tabulated instances measures recall and search together. It can say “arm X, at budget B, matched the tabulated length on k of 12 pairs”. It cannot say anything new about Golomb rulers, and a miss says nothing about whether a shorter ruler exists. The honest verbs are verified, matched the tabulated length, and did not reach it within 2000 evaluations.

There is no dataset, only an instance and an oracle

The modality is none: no rows, no columns, no train and test split. What the study reads is one tiny prepared file, data/prepared/instance.json, produced by the deterministic prepare.py and hashed at the DATA gate. It declares the two lanes (development orders 8–11, sealed orders 12–13), three trials per order, a budget of 2000 candidate evaluations, a batch size of 10 for the LLM arm, and the seed blocks. The “split” is the pair of lanes. The DATA gate therefore ran a verifier card in place of a leakage audit, and its call was go, with cautions (the gate record, not this page, holds the status).

The value-pattern check, applied to an object with no columns

The rule is never to trust a type, so every scalar in instance.json was inspected by value. All counts and lengths are JSON integers: no numbers stored as strings, no booleans, no sentinels such as -1 or NA. The optima keys are strings of integers that search.py converts with int(). One convention to know: order 1 has length 0 by convention, and no lane uses it.

Where the answer key comes from, said honestly

The lengths compared against are OEIS A003022 values for orders 8–13 (ref:oeis_a003022). They are pinned inside the verifier (ORACLE), and the verifier refuses an instance.json that disagrees with any pinned field, because the file sits where the mutable search.py has just run with write access. Who established that nothing shorter exists is a literature fact this study did not re-run: the data card records that the OEIS entry gives no per-term reference for these orders, links Shearer's tables, and credits distributed.net only for far larger orders. So “tabulated optimum” means “the OEIS value, from exhaustive searches by others”. What the DATA gate did check independently is attainability: tabulated rulers transcribed by hand for orders 8–13 were accepted by the verifier with exactly the table lengths.

The gotchas that shaped the study

  1. The sealed orders are public. “Sealed” protects against adaptive tuning of search.py (one run per arm, a mandatory dry run first). It does not make the sealed orders unseen by the model. A sealed LLM match would have been consistent with recall, which is why the study registers the first-batch signature beside the sealed prediction.
  2. Two holes found by an adversarial review, then closed. The artifact named its own lane, so a development run could have submitted a sealed-lane artifact; and the optima lived in a file the searcher could rewrite. The verifier now maps the notary's evaluation kind to the lane and carries the pinned oracle.
  3. Budget parity is self-reported. The verifier enforces that each pair spent exactly the budget, but the counter lives in the mutable file. The independent record for the LLM arm is the call ledger.
  4. The budget is matched in verifier calls, not in information or time. The annealer sees one verdict per candidate; the LLM sees one text block per 10. Every comparison is phrased “at a matched number of candidate evaluations”.
  5. No lane field is a partition. With split.kind: none there is no row split to fingerprint; the lane is guarded by the verifier's evaluation-kind check and its pinned oracle instead, and the engine's split-fingerprint check is advisory for this study.

Controls on the verifier

Before any lane run, the verifier was exercised with hand-made artifacts in a scratch directory. It rejected planted invalid rulers, forged lengths, wrong-lane artifacts and a tampered oracle, and it accepted the hand-transcribed tabulated rulers, scoring 12 of 12 on the development lane and 6 of 6 on the sealed lane. A script in sweeps/ re-runs nine of those refusals against the final verifier. Two caveats the referee asked this page to carry: the data card labels these controls the other way round from the conventional usage in findings (the gate-hashed card is left as written), and the scratch artifacts are not pinned, so their record is the card's text. These controls test the verifier. They say nothing about either arm.

How to read a registered journey

Both tracks are registered: each run is a pre-declared cell, measured or crash, never a keep or a discard. So there is no frontier to climb. The “journey” is the sequence of cells, the two crashes that interrupted one of them, and the separate sealed confirmation cell. The step line of the engine's trajectory plot is empty by design; what matters is where the squares, the crosses and the star fall.

Development evidence (orders 8–11) and sealed confirmation evidence (orders 12–13) are different partitions and are labelled separately everywhere below.

The search track

One development cell measured the annealer (E0001), and one sealed cell measured it again on the sealed orders, once, after a dry run (E0005). Nothing about the mutable surface changed between them: the notary recorded an empty candidate diff on both, and section 6 shows the same bytes under both run ids.

The llm track, and the two crashes

The model arm needed four attempts at one development cell. E0002 died on an HTTP 429 rate limit from the provider after 613 calls. The transport was made to wait out rate limits and the concurrency was lowered; E0003 then died on a bare connection reset after 523 live calls plus 613 answered from E0002's shard. The transport was made to retry dropped connections, and the same pre-registered cell ran to completion as E0004. Neither crash was a bug in the ruler logic, both are kept in the ledger as crashes with an NA metric, and each fix was a dated lead decision with the contract re-recorded. No registered prediction changed.

The caveat this leaves is that E0004 answered a large share of its requests from the crashed runs' shards. Those are genuine recorded responses to byte-identical requests, but they make E0004 partly the same sample as the crashed runs, so only the salted re-query is a fully independent second draw (claim C12).

What each cell measured, pair by pair

The count hides the shape. Plotting each (order, trial) pair as best verified length against the tabulated length separates the two arms cleanly:

Three things are visible without any test. The annealer's gap grows monotonically with order, as the method card's prior predicted, so its zero is hardness growth at a fixed budget, not a defect. The LLM arm is all-or-none within each development order, which is why the pair-level contrast overstates its evidence (claim C11). And on the sealed orders the LLM arm did not merely fail to match: it produced no valid ruler, so its row of crosses has no length to compare.

  • Matched budget: a dated decision fixed the budget in candidate evaluations, 2000 per order and trial, accepting that the LLM spends 10 per proposal.

Scope of the referee’s verdict. It was recorded on the study record before this page existed. It does not cover this tutorial or its figures. The notes attached to it are carried into the claims below: C7 is re-scoped by erratum E1; the mechanism readings are untested hypotheses; the budget was matched in verifier calls only; usd is unrecorded, not zero; a search miss is never evidence that a match is out of reach; and exactly one model snapshot was queried.

The verdicts

  • The classical search matched 0 of 12 development pairs and 0 of 6 sealed pairs (C1, C5, both confirmed). Its mean gap grew from 5.667 length units at order 8 to 35.333 at order 11, and a re-execution reproduced the count exactly. This describes this annealer at 2000 evaluations only; a published heuristic such as ref:dotu2005 was not run, and a miss here says nothing about whether a match is within reach at another budget.
  • The LLM arm matched 6 of 12 development pairs (C2, exploratory), all three trials of orders 8 and 11 and none of orders 9 and 10. P2 had registered at least 9, so it is refuted. A salted re-query of every call reproduced the count of 6 but not the pair-level detail.
  • The contrast is a count, not a rate (C3, exploratory). The development difference is +6 pairs. The exact McNemar p is 0.03125 if the 12 pairs are independent, which does not clear the Bonferroni level of 0.025 for the two arm contrasts, and 0.5 if the four orders are the unit. The orders, not the pairs, are the honest unit, because the three trials of an order sent byte-identical first requests.
  • On the sealed orders neither arm matched (C5, confirmed): the LLM arm produced no verified ruler at all. The sealed lane was read once per arm, and the sealed cells could not be replicated by design (the engine refuses a second look at the sealed partition), so C1 and C5 rest on development replications that confirm the instrument, not the sealed counts themselves.
  • Predictions: two supported (P1, P4), three refuted (P2, P3, P5), each refutation answered by a dated decision line (C6, a ledger fact).

Surprise 1: the recall signature did not appear

The registered recall test was a match in the first proposal batch, before any verifier feedback. It was seen in 1 of 12 pairs (P3 asked for at least 6). Five of the six matched pairs first reached the tabulated length after feedback, at proposals as late as 74 of 200 (C4).

The next two subsections are the closest thing this study has to a mechanism, and both are hypotheses.

Surprise 2 (an untested hypothesis): the matches look like retrieval of printed rows

Every sentence in this subsection is a hypothesis of class mechanism-interpretation, strength exploratory. No experiment in this study was designed to test it (C7, C8).

  • Observed. At order 8 every matched ruler is the printed row 0 1 4 9 15 22 32 34. At order 11 every matched ruler is the printed row 0 1 4 13 28 33 47 54 64 70 72. At order 10 all three bests are the first ten marks of that 11-mark row, a valid ruler by inheritance at length 70 against the tabulated 55, and no order-10 proposal ever reached the tabulated 10-mark row.
  • Erratum E1 on C7. The locked sentence calls the tabulated optimum “unique”. That is wrong as stated: at order 8 it is unique only up to reflection, and at order 11 there are two tabulated rulers up to reflection. Across every proposal in the ledger, the only rulers at the tabulated length are the table’s printed rows in their printed orientation; the mirror images and the second 11-mark ruler were never proposed. Identity therefore carries weak, post-hoc information that leans toward retrieval. It is not a test, and C7 stays exploratory.
  • Why it stays a hypothesis. The same facts fit a short local search that converges on a tabulated length. Only a contamination control (an instance with no public answer) could separate the two, and the study ran none.
  • The order-9 hole (C8, also a hypothesis). Order 9 produced no valid ruler in 600 proposals, while orders 10 and 11 did. One reading is that proposals anchor on extending the printed 8-mark row, which usually repeats a difference. But the first nine marks of the printed 11-mark row form a valid 9-mark ruler and were never proposed, so truncating the longer row is not a general strategy of this model.

Surprise 3: the sealed LLM cell produced no valid ruler

The LLM arm produced no valid ruler at order 12 or 13, not merely no match (invalid best in 6 of 6 pairs). That claim does not rest on the searcher’s self-report: the synthesis recounts it from the pinned call-ledger shard with its own checker, reading every bracketed integer list in every reply, and finds none that is a valid ruler. Between a fifth and three in ten of the replies could not be parsed at all, at every order:

One honesty note on sources: for the salted re-query, the first-batch count and the primary count are the verifier’s, but its valid-ruler and unparsed counts are searcher-reported, and the replica’s per-pair table was not kept (C14).

Surprise 4: the compute behind a “matched” budget

The budget was matched in verifier calls only. What it hid is the cost on the other axes (C10): the LLM arm took roughly four orders of magnitude more wall-clock than the annealer, and carried millions of tokens through the provider.

usd is unrecorded, not zero. The study’s calls block declared no price, so every recorded usd reads 0 (claim C13). The dollar cost of the live model calls is therefore unrecorded; live token counts are recorded, so a price applied later can be computed from them. The call total is lower than the data card’s early estimate because the sealed cell cannot be re-queried by design and the development cell was re-queried once.

What the matched rulers establish, and what they do not

  • A verified ruler of length certifies only the upper bound . The matched rulers give and , both already the OEIS A003022 values (ref:oeis_a003022). The study establishes nothing new about any Golomb length (C16).
  • The unmatched verified rulers give weaker bounds than the table already holds.
  • No lower bound, and no statement that a match is out of reach for any proposer. The LLM arm’s failure to write a valid 12- or 13-mark ruler describes one snapshot under one prompt, not the difficulty of writing one down; explicit constructions exist (ref:singer1938, ref:atkinson1986).
  • One model snapshot. Only qwen-flash-2025-07-28 was queried, at temperature 0.7, as served on the study date. Every LLM statement is about that snapshot.

Controls that exist, and controls that are missing

Present: the exact verifier with a pinned oracle, the table of tabulated lengths, and a ledger cross-check (every pair has exactly 200 calls, and the stored first batch equals the ledger’s first reply in every pair). Missing, by design of the two-arm contract and with both phase allowances spent: a contamination control (an instance with no public answer), a no-feedback LLM arm (the same prompt resampled without verdicts, to separate feedback-steered repair from resampling), a compute-matched or stronger classical arm, a second snapshot or temperature, and an empirical blind-proposal null. Each missing control is the reason a specific claim above is a hypothesis and not a finding.

Why this section exists

The study’s conclusions are only as good as two small programs: the searcher that proposes and the verifier that judges. This section walks the executed source of both. For the searcher the page includes the exact bytes each named run executed, read from that run’s recorded candidate commit, not the file lying on disk (a registered track restores the mutable surface after every run, so the disk copy names no run). The verifier is outside the mutable surface and is shown as the declared verifier with its pinned hash.

The searcher, as executed

search.py is the study’s whole mutable surface and holds both arms, selected by the track. The four listings below are the same file included at four runs. Their provenance lines print the run id, evaluation kind, track, commit and sha256; the four hashes are identical, because the surface was never edited between runs. That identity is itself the point: the classical arm and the LLM arm ran on the same bytes, and the sealed runs ran the code the development runs ran.

Classical arm, development cell (E0001) and sealed cell (E0005).

search.py · executed by E0001 (development, track search) at commit f8efcf87c00e · sha256 b3188a3e6eee… 
"""The searcher (the mutable surface): two arms that propose Golomb rulers for verify.py.

A Golomb ruler with n marks is a list of integers 0 = a1 < ... < an whose pairwise
differences are all distinct; its length is an, and shorter is better. For every
(order, trial) pair of the lane this run draws, an arm gets the same budget of
candidate evaluations — ONE candidate ruler checked by this file's private
`_is_golomb` is ONE evaluation, whatever produced it — and keeps the shortest valid
ruler it found:

  search  randomized construction + simulated annealing on the mark positions
          (KLEIN_TRACK=search)
  llm     qwen-flash proposes batches of rulers as JSON DATA (never code), each
          batch told the checker's verdicts on the previous one, every request
          through the call ledger (KLEIN_TRACK=llm)

The lane is KLEIN_EVALUATION_KIND: development -> development_orders, final_test ->
sealed_orders; the sealed rehearsal (KLEIN_SEALED_DRYRUN=1) runs the development
orders and prints `sealed_dryrun: 1`. Orders, trials, budget, batch size and seed
blocks come from data/prepared/instance.json (hashed at the DATA gate). The known
optima are read for BOOK-KEEPING ONLY — the provisional count printed below and the
index of the first optimal ruler; no search decision and no prompt uses them.

The run's number is provisional: the declared verifier (verify.py — outside this
surface, sharing no code with it, hashed at METHOD) recomputes `optima_matched` and
`first_batch_matches` from the artifact printed under `solution:`, and decides.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

SEALED_DRYRUN = os.environ.get("KLEIN_SEALED_DRYRUN") == "1"

# Smoke: the first development order, one trial, a tiny budget (a shape check, not evidence).
SMOKE_BUDGET = {"search": 200, "llm": 30}

# --- the search arm -----------------------------------------------------------
SA_T0 = 1.0           # starting temperature, in units of "repeated differences"

SA_T_MIN = 0.05

P_CONFLICTED = 0.85   # move a mark that takes part in a repeated difference
P_LOCAL = 0.5         # ... by a small shift (else: anywhere free on the ruler)

# --- the llm arm --------------------------------------------------------------
LLM_PARAMS = {"temperature": 0.7, "max_tokens": 1024, "enable_thinking": False}
SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
    "You propose Golomb rulers as data. A Golomb ruler with n marks is a list of n "
    "integers that starts at 0, is strictly increasing, and has all pairwise "
    "differences distinct. Its length is its last mark, and a shorter ruler is "
    "better. Reply with JSON data only: never code, never an explanation."
)


# --- the searcher's own checker (never the verifier) -----------------------------


class Budget:
    """Candidate evaluations for one (order, trial): every `_is_golomb` call spends one."""

    def __init__(self, limit: int) -> None:
        self.limit = int(limit)
        self.spent = 0

    def exhausted(self) -> bool:
        return self.spent >= self.limit

    def spend(self) -> None:
        if self.spent >= self.limit:
            raise RuntimeError(f"evaluation budget overspent ({self.limit})")
        self.spent += 1


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Verdict:
    valid: bool
    reason: str                    # "valid", or why the candidate is not a valid ruler
    length: int | None             # the last mark, when the candidate is a well-formed mark list
    first_repeat: int | None       # the first repeated difference, pairs scanned (i < j) by j then i
    repeats: int                   # differences that repeat an earlier one
    conflicted: tuple[int, ...]    # mark indices that take part in a repeated difference


def _is_golomb(marks: Any, n: int, budget: Budget) -> Verdict:
    """The searcher's private checker. Each call is one evaluation of the budget."""
    budget.spend()
    if marks is None:
        return Verdict(False, "missing", None, None, 0, ())
    if not isinstance(marks, list) or not all(
        isinstance(m, int) and not isinstance(m, bool) for m in marks
    ):
        return Verdict(False, "not a list of integers", None, None, 0, ())
    if len(marks) != n:
        return Verdict(False, f"has {len(marks)} marks, needs {n}", None, None, 0, ())
    if marks[0] != 0:
        return Verdict(False, "does not start at 0", None, None, 0, ())
    if any(b <= a for a, b in zip(marks, marks[1:], strict=False)):
        return Verdict(False, "not strictly increasing", None, None, 0, ())
    owner: dict[int, tuple[int, int]] = {}
    repeats, first, conflicted = 0, None, set()
    for j in range(1, n):
        for i in range(j):
            d = marks[j] - marks[i]
            earlier = owner.get(d)
            if earlier is None:
                owner[d] = (i, j)
                continue
            repeats += 1
            first = d if first is None else first
            conflicted.update((i, j, *earlier))
    if repeats:
        return Verdict(False, f"difference {first} repeats", marks[-1], first, repeats,
                       tuple(sorted(conflicted)))
    return Verdict(True, "valid", marks[-1], None, 0, ())


# --- arm 1: randomized construction + simulated annealing ------------------------


def _random_ruler(n: int, length: int, rng: random.Random) -> list[int]:
    return [0, *sorted(rng.sample(range(1, length), n - 2)), length]


def _shrink(marks: list[int], step: int, rng: random.Random) -> list[int]:
    """Cut `step` empty unit cells at random: differences on one side of a cut survive."""
    marks = list(marks)
    for _ in range(step):
        occupied = set(marks)
        cut = rng.choice([c for c in range(1, marks[-1]) if c not in occupied])
        marks = [m - 1 if m > cut else m for m in marks]
    return marks


def _move(marks: list[int], verdict: Verdict, rng: random.Random) -> list[int]:
    """Relocate one interior mark (the ends 0 and L stay): the length is unchanged."""
    n, length = len(marks), marks[-1]
    interior = [i for i in verdict.conflicted if 0 < i < n - 1]
    if interior and rng.random() < P_CONFLICTED:
        i = rng.choice(interior)
    else:
        i = rng.randrange(1, n - 1)
    occupied = set(marks)
    while True:
        if rng.random() < P_LOCAL:
            p = marks[i] + rng.choice((-3, -2, -1, 1, 2, 3))
        else:
            p = rng.randrange(1, length)
        if 0 < p < length and p not in occupied:
            break
    return sorted([*marks[:i], *marks[i + 1:], p])


def search_pair(n: int, seed: int, limit: int, optimum: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """One (order, trial): the shortest valid ruler found within `limit` evaluations.

    Construction: both ends fixed at 0 and n*n, n-2 interior marks at random (sparse enough that a few
    moves make it valid). Then repeatedly: aim one length shorter than the best valid
    ruler (an adaptive step, doubling while successes come fast), start from the best
    with empty cells cut out, and anneal the interior marks to remove repeated
    differences; restart from the best after SA_PATIENCE evaluations without a valid
    ruler. Stops at the budget, or at the trivial bound n(n-1)/2 (a perfect ruler).
    """
    if n < 3:
        raise ValueError("the search arm needs at least 3 marks")
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    budget = Budget(limit)
    floor = n * (n - 1) // 2
    best: list[int] | None = None
    best_at = first_optimal_at = None
    state: list[int] | None = None
    state_verdict: Verdict | None = None
    step, since_valid, since_start, restarts = 1, 0, 0, 0
    temperature = SA_T0
    while not budget.exhausted():
        if best is not None and best[-1] <= floor:
            break  # n(n-1)/2 distinct positive differences: nothing shorter exists
        if state is None:
            if best is None:
                candidate = _random_ruler(n, n * n, rng)
            else:
                candidate = _shrink(best, min(step, best[-1] - floor), rng)
        else:
            candidate = _move(state, state_verdict, rng)
        verdict = _is_golomb(candidate, n, budget)
        since_valid += 1
        if verdict.valid:
            if best is None or candidate[-1] < best[-1]:
                best, best_at = candidate, budget.spent
                if first_optimal_at is None and candidate[-1] == optimum:
                    first_optimal_at = budget.spent
            step = min(2 * step, n) if since_valid <= n else 1
            state, state_verdict = None, None
            since_valid, since_start, temperature = 0, 0, SA_T0
            continue
        if (
            state_verdict is None
            or verdict.repeats <= state_verdict.repeats
            or rng.random() < math.exp((state_verdict.repeats - verdict.repeats) / temperature)
        ):
            state, state_verdict = candidate, verdict
        temperature = max(SA_T_MIN, temperature * SA_COOLING)
        since_start += 1
        if since_start >= SA_PATIENCE:
            state, state_verdict = None, None
            step, since_start, temperature = 1, 0, SA_T0
            restarts += 1
    return {
        "best": best,
        "best_length": None if best is None else best[-1],
        "evaluations": budget.spent,
        "best_found_at_evaluation": best_at,
        "first_optimal_evaluation": first_optimal_at,
        "restarts": restarts,
    }


def run_search(orders: list[int], trials: int, limit: int, lane_seed: int,
               optima: dict[int, int]) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], dict[str, float]]:
    pairs = []
    for n in orders:
        for trial in range(trials):
            seed = lane_seed + n * 100 + trial
            pairs.append({"order": n, "trial": trial, "seed": seed,
                          **search_pair(n, seed, limit, optima[n])})
    return pairs, {"restarts": float(sum(p["restarts"] for p in pairs))}


# --- arm 2: the LLM proposes rulers as data -------------------------------------

_INNER_LIST = re.compile(r"\[[^\[\]]*\]")


def _parse_batch(text: str, batch: int) -> tuple[list[Any], bool]:
    """Exactly `batch` entries (None = missing) and whether the reply was one JSON list.

    The outermost [...] span is read as JSON (this strips code fences and any prose
    around it). A reply cut off mid-list falls back to every complete inner list.
    Nothing is repaired: an entry that is not already a valid ruler is an invalid
    evaluation, and a missing entry still spends its evaluation.
    """
    entries: list[Any] | None = None
    start, end = text.find("["), text.rfind("]")
    if start != -1 and end > start:
        try:
            value = json.loads(text[start:end + 1])
        except ValueError:
            value = None
        if isinstance(value, list):
            if value and all(isinstance(v, int) and not isinstance(v, bool) for v in value):
                value = [value]  # one bare ruler
            entries = value
    strict = entries is not None
    if entries is None:
        entries = []
        for chunk in _INNER_LIST.findall(text):
            try:
                entries.append(json.loads(chunk))
            except ValueError:
                continue
    entries = entries[:batch]
    return entries + [None] * (batch - len(entries)), strict


def _show(entry: Any) -> str:
    if entry is None:
        return "(no ruler)"
    text = json.dumps(entry)
    return text if len(text) <= 160 else text[:157] + "..."


def _describe(verdict: Verdict) -> str:
    if verdict.valid:
        return f"valid, length {verdict.length}"
    if verdict.first_repeat is not None:
        return f"invalid, length {verdict.length}, difference {verdict.first_repeat} repeats"
    return f"invalid, {verdict.reason}"


def _messages(n: int, k: int, proposals: int, batch: int,
              previous: list[tuple[Any, Verdict]] | None,
              best_length: int | None) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    lines = [
        f"Propose exactly {batch} candidate Golomb rulers with {n} marks each.",
        f"Every ruler must start at 0, be strictly increasing, contain exactly {n} "
        f"integers, and have all {n * (n - 1) // 2} pairwise differences distinct. "
        "Shorter is better: the length of a ruler is its last mark.",
        f"This is proposal {k} of {proposals}.",
    ]
    if previous is not None:
        lines += ["", "The verifier's verdicts on your previous batch:"]
        lines += [f"{i}. {_show(entry)}: {_describe(verdict)}"
                  for i, (entry, verdict) in enumerate(previous, start=1)]
        lines.append(f"Best valid length so far: {best_length}." if best_length is not None
                     else "No valid ruler so far.")
    lines += ["", f"Reply with a JSON list of {batch} lists of integers and nothing else."]
    return [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT},
            {"role": "user", "content": "\n".join(lines)}]


class _Aborted(RuntimeError):
    """Another (order, trial) loop failed; this one stops before its next request."""


def llm_pair(ledger: Any, n: int, trial: int, limit: int, batch: int, optimum: int,
             abort: threading.Event) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """One (order, trial): `limit // batch` sequential proposals, each fed back the last."""
    budget = Budget(limit)
    proposals = limit // batch
    best: list[int] | None = None
    best_at = first_optimal = None
    first_batch: list[Any] | None = None
    previous: list[tuple[Any, Verdict]] | None = None
    valid = unparsed = 0
    for k in range(1, proposals + 1):
        if abort.is_set():
            raise _Aborted(f"order {n} trial {trial} stopped at proposal {k}")
        reply = ledger.chat(_messages(n, k, proposals, batch, previous,
                                      None if best is None else best[-1]),
                            sample=trial, **LLM_PARAMS)
        entries, strict = _parse_batch(reply, batch)
        unparsed += not strict
        verdicts = [_is_golomb(entry, n, budget) for entry in entries]
        if k == 1:
            first_batch = [entry if isinstance(entry, list) else None for entry in entries]
        for entry, verdict in zip(entries, verdicts, strict=True):
            if not verdict.valid:
                continue
            valid += 1
            if best is None or entry[-1] < best[-1]:
                best, best_at = list(entry), k
            if first_optimal is None and entry[-1] == optimum:
                first_optimal = k
        previous = list(zip(entries, verdicts, strict=True))
    return {
        "best": best,
        "best_length": None if best is None else best[-1],
        "evaluations": budget.spent,
        "proposals": proposals,
        "best_found_at_proposal": best_at,
        "first_optimal_proposal": first_optimal,
        "valid_rulers": valid,
        "unparsed_replies": unparsed,
        "first_batch": first_batch,
    }


def _smoke_reply(n: int) -> str:
    """A fenced JSON batch for KLEIN_SMOKE=1: one entry per parse/verdict path, then padding."""
    sidon = [2 ** i - 1 for i in range(n)]  # 2^j - 2^i are all distinct: a valid ruler
    batch = [
        sidon,
        [2 * m for m in sidon],             # valid, longer
        [m + 1 for m in sidon],             # does not start at 0
        list(range(0, 2 * n, 2)),           # difference 2 repeats
        sidon[:-1],                         # wrong mark count
        [0, *sidon[:0:-1]],                 # not strictly increasing
        "x",                                # not a list
    ]
    return "Here are the rulers:\n```json\n" + json.dumps(batch) + "\n```"


def run_llm(orders: list[int], trials: int, limit: int, batch: int,
            optima: dict[int, int]) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], dict[str, float], dict[str, Any]]:
    from kleinlib.calls import CallLedger

    if limit % batch:
        raise SystemExit(f"budget {limit} is not a multiple of the batch {batch}")
    # The sealed rehearsal replays the development cell from the ledger and must
    # spend nothing: offline, a request the ledger cannot answer is a crash.
    overrides = {"offline": True} if SEALED_DRYRUN else {}
    jobs = [(n, trial) for n in orders for trial in range(trials)]
    abort = threading.Event()
    results: dict[tuple[int, int], dict[str, Any]] = {}
    error: BaseException | None = None
    with CallLedger.from_contract(".", smoke_response=_smoke_reply(orders[0]), **overrides) as ledger:
        # Proposals within a trial are sequential (each carries the last batch's
        # verdicts); the (order, trial) loops are independent and run side by side,
        # calls.max_workers at a time. Each loop passes its trial index as `sample`,
        # so the trials are distinct requests, not cached copies of one another.
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=min(ledger.max_workers, len(jobs))) as pool:
            futures = {pool.submit(llm_pair, ledger, n, trial, limit, batch, optima[n], abort): (n, trial)
                       for n, trial in jobs}
            for future in as_completed(futures):
                exc = future.exception()
                if exc is None:
                    results[futures[future]] = future.result()
                elif error is None:
                    error = exc
                    abort.set()
        meta = {"model": ledger.model, "base_url": ledger.base_url, "params": LLM_PARAMS,
                "batch": batch, "proposals_per_trial": limit // batch,
                "system_prompt": SYSTEM_PROMPT}
    if error is not None:
        raise error
    pairs = [{"order": n, "trial": trial, "sample": trial, **results[(n, trial)]} for n, trial in jobs]
    extra = {
        "valid_rulers": float(sum(p["valid_rulers"] for p in pairs)),
        "unparsed_replies": float(sum(p["unparsed_replies"] for p in pairs)),
        **ledger.summary(),
    }
    return pairs, extra, meta


# --- the run ------------------------------------------------------------------


def _artifact_path() -> Path:
    if SMOKE:
        return Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="klein-smoke-")) / f"solution_SMOKE_{TRACK}.json"
    if SEALED_DRYRUN:
        # Filed with the rehearsal's own state commit (sweeps/), so the tree the
        # sealed run needs stays clean; tables/ holds only real runs' artifacts.
        return Path("sweeps") / f"solution_DRYRUN_{TRACK}.json"
    return Path("tables") / f"solution_{EXPERIMENT_ID}.json"


def main() -> None:
    t0 = time.time()
    kind = os.environ.get("KLEIN_EVALUATION_KIND") or ("development" if SMOKE else None)
    if EXPERIMENT_ID is None or kind is None or TRACK is None:
        raise SystemExit("run through `klein run-one` (or KLEIN_SMOKE=1 KLEIN_TRACK=<arm> for a shape check)")
    if TRACK not in ARMS:
        raise SystemExit(f"KLEIN_TRACK={TRACK!r}: this study's arms are {ARMS}")
    if kind not in {"development", "final_test"}:
        raise RuntimeError(f"invalid KLEIN_EVALUATION_KIND={kind!r}")
    instance = json.loads(Path("data/prepared/instance.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    lane = "sealed" if kind == "final_test" else "development"
    if kind == "final_test" and SEALED_DRYRUN:
        print("sealed_dryrun: 1")
        lane = "development"
    orders = [int(n) for n in instance[f"{lane}_orders"]]
    trials = int(instance["trials"])
    limit = int(instance["budget_evaluations"])
    batch = int(instance["llm_batch"])
    lane_seed = int(instance["seed_blocks"][lane])
    optima = {int(n): int(length) for n, length in instance["optima"].items()}
    if SMOKE:
        orders, trials, limit = orders[:1], 1, SMOKE_BUDGET[TRACK]

    payload: dict[str, Any] = {
        "problem": "golomb-ruler", "arm": TRACK, "experiment": EXPERIMENT_ID, "lane": lane,
        "sealed_dryrun": SEALED_DRYRUN, "orders": orders, "trials": trials,
        "budget_evaluations": limit,
    }
    if TRACK == "search":
        pairs, extra = run_search(orders, trials, limit, lane_seed, optima)
        payload["seed_block"] = lane_seed
    else:
        pairs, extra, payload["llm"] = run_llm(orders, trials, limit, batch, optima)
    payload["pairs"] = pairs

    matched = sum(p["best_length"] == optima[p["order"]] for p in pairs)
    first_batch = sum(p.get("first_optimal_proposal") == 1 for p in pairs)

    out = _artifact_path()
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=1, sort_keys=True) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"solution: {out.as_posix()}")
    print(f"artifact: {out.as_posix()}")

    lane_fingerprint = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(
        {"lane": lane, "orders": orders, "trials": trials, "budget": limit, "seed_block": lane_seed},
        sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
    evaluate_scalar(
        float(matched), exp_id=EXPERIMENT_ID, metric_name="optima_matched", metric_goal="higher",
        extra={
            "first_batch_matches": float(first_batch),
            "pairs": float(len(pairs)),
            "evaluations": float(sum(p["evaluations"] for p in pairs)),
            "sealed_lane": 1.0 if lane == "sealed" else 0.0,
            **extra,
        },
        split_fingerprint=lane_fingerprint, t0=t0, study_dir=None if SMOKE else ".",
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""The searcher (the mutable surface): two arms that propose Golomb rulers for verify.py.

A Golomb ruler with n marks is a list of integers 0 = a1 < ... < an whose pairwise
differences are all distinct; its length is an, and shorter is better. For every
(order, trial) pair of the lane this run draws, an arm gets the same budget of
candidate evaluations — ONE candidate ruler checked by this file's private
`_is_golomb` is ONE evaluation, whatever produced it — and keeps the shortest valid
ruler it found:

  search  randomized construction + simulated annealing on the mark positions
          (KLEIN_TRACK=search)
  llm     qwen-flash proposes batches of rulers as JSON DATA (never code), each
          batch told the checker's verdicts on the previous one, every request
          through the call ledger (KLEIN_TRACK=llm)

The lane is KLEIN_EVALUATION_KIND: development -> development_orders, final_test ->
sealed_orders; the sealed rehearsal (KLEIN_SEALED_DRYRUN=1) runs the development
orders and prints `sealed_dryrun: 1`. Orders, trials, budget, batch size and seed
blocks come from data/prepared/instance.json (hashed at the DATA gate). The known
optima are read for BOOK-KEEPING ONLY — the provisional count printed below and the
index of the first optimal ruler; no search decision and no prompt uses them.

The run's number is provisional: the declared verifier (verify.py — outside this
surface, sharing no code with it, hashed at METHOD) recomputes `optima_matched` and
`first_batch_matches` from the artifact printed under `solution:`, and decides.
